messages:

Subject: Post-call recap: Acme Health private/VPC deployment constraints and next steps

Hi Lisa / Rajiv — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Pain points and drivers you shared:
- Data residency & regulatory: patient data must remain in Acme-managed VPCs and meet HIPAA-adjacent controls.
- Air-gap requirement for certain workloads: images/artifacts must be installable offline for some environments.
- Strict egress rules: nodes cannot have unrestricted outbound internet; all traffic goes through corporate proxy or NAT.
- Key management & auditability: centralized KMS/HSM integration and long-term audit logs required.

Goals we discussed:
- Run Redwood Private inside Acme VPC with optional air-gapped install for test/production clusters.
- Ensure no uncontrolled egress; support for proxy/NAT or peered control plane.
- KMS integration for key rotation and audit exports to your SIEM.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Private deployment modes: (1) Private control plane + managed peering, (2) Fully air-gapped on-prem package for environments with zero egress.
- KMS/HSM integrations and configurable audit log exports.
- Support for offline image install (air-gap) plus an airgap preflight checklist and install package.

Network & infra asks (what we need from you):
1) Current network diagram (attached) and contact for firewall/VPN team.
2) Whether you prefer VPN or AWS VPC peering for the control-plane connectivity option.
3) List of allowed outbound proxy/NAT egress rules (if nodes must use corporate proxy).
4) Estimated cluster sizes and latency SLOs (tokens/sec, concurrency) so we can size GPUs and KV cache storage.

Attachments: acme-vpc-reqs.pdf (network checklist) and acme-network-diagram.png (we sketched during call).

Next steps / timeline:
- Action: Marissa to send updated network checklist + airgap checklist (attached) — today.
- Action: Acme to share network diagram and firewall contact — by Fri, Sep 4.
- Action: Technical call with David (SE) + your firewall team — propose Tue, Sep 8, 10:00am PT. Please confirm.

If anything here is incorrect or missing, call it out and I’ll update. Thanks again — excited to help you get Private deployed with the controls you need.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

https://redwood.inference.com

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- On egress: for our production clusters we cannot allow any outbound connections directly from compute nodes to the public internet. All outbound must go through our corporate proxy or NAT with IP-allowlisting.
- Air-gap: for some regulated projects we need an offline install path (no inbound/outbound during install). We expect to pull artifacts via a secured jumpbox.
- Control plane: we are leaning toward peering to reduce latency, but our security team will confirm.

Question: will Redwood require periodic phone-home for model updates/telemetry, or can we opt into a fully offline mode and receive periodic signed artifact bundles?

IT contact for firewall/proxy questions: it@acmehealth.com (please loop them into the technical call).

I can share our internal network diagram and firewall rules by end of day Friday.

Thanks Rajiv — great notes. Short answers to your questions and updated asks below.

- Telemetry / "phone home": Redwood supports both models. For production air-gapped installs we can provide signed artifact bundles and an offline install path (no phone-home). For private deployments with a peered control plane we typically keep a minimal telemetry channel for health + billing; that can be routed through your proxy or using peered connectivity.
- Artifacts & updates: we will prepare a signed artifact bundle and an airgap install package for your offline environments.
- Peering vs VPN: peering gives better network performance; VPN is easier for initial POC. We'll document both approaches.

I've attached an updated airgap checklist (redwood-airgap-checklist.pdf) and a short list of minimal endpoints/ports we need for the peered control-plane option. If you prefer fully offline, you can ignore the minimal endpoints list.

Rajiv / Marissa — quick technical note ahead of the Sep 8 call.

A few specifics to help your firewall/proxy team plan: 
- Minimal outbound endpoints (peered control-plane option): 3 CIDR ranges we manage for control-plane traffic (we'll provide exact CIDRs in the pre-call doc). All traffic is TLS 443.
- Proxy/NAT: nodes can use your corporate proxy for outbound. If you use an HTTP proxy with authentication, we'll provide a proxy helper and instructions.
- SSH: we do not require SSH from the internet to worker nodes in production. For install/debug, we support SSH to a bastion (jumpbox) on your side — recommend opening port 22 only between bastion and worker subnets.
- Airgap install: we'll deliver a signed artifact tarball (models + runtime) and a separate installer binary. Size: expect ~45-60GB for initial model artifacts depending on model choice. Ensure workers have at least 200GB ephemeral storage and 1TB persistent for KV cache + logs for larger clusters.
- Peering vs VPN: peering reduces latency; VPN is acceptable for POC. If you do peering, ensure route table updates and cross-account IAM roles are in place.
- Audit logs & KMS: we support sending audit logs to a S3 bucket in your account and integrating with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping.

Action items for our side: David to produce a one-page minimal-ports-and-cidrs doc + an airgap preflight checklist before the Sep 8 call.

Rajiv — could you share the contact for your firewall team (name + email) so we can include them on the invite and the pre-call doc?

Thanks,
David Kim
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
